identity.display_name: Audi R8 LMS GT3 Evo II
identity.real_world_identity_notes: Audi identifies the Evo II as the second evolution of the R8 LMS GT3. The exact base AMS2 identity was guided-tested; the Low Downforce identity is an explicit aero-package alias inheriting the base controls and was not separately tested.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a closed GT/Formula rim without an integrated display or wheel-mounted shift lights.

notes: The base car moved from rest without physical clutch input; the underlying simulator mechanism was not established.
Six paddle-selected gears, clutchless no-lift upshifts, and clutchless downshifts with automatic blip were directly established.
Automatic cut is a medium-confidence manual observation based on a brief throttle-graph interruption during an upshift while pedal input was maintained.
The Low Downforce identity inherits base controls as an explicit untested aero-package assumption.

confidence.basis: Exact identity and most user-facing controls were directly verified; manufacturer lineage supports the six-speed paddle-sequential architecture. Automatic cut is a separately disclosed medium-confidence manual telemetry-graph observation.

claims.basis: Official simulator and manufacturer sources agree with the exact live telemetry identity and class.
Low Downforce is an exact observed identity whose controls explicitly inherit the tested base as an aero-package assumption.
Audi lineage documentation and direct exercise of all six paddle-selected gears agree.

notes: Low Downforce is an explicit inherited alias and was not separately live-tested.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
